title: Four-loop perturbative Konishi from strings and finite size effects for multiparticle states
journal: Nucl. Phys. B (DOI 10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2008.08.020; volume/page not verified)
claim: Four-loop planar Konishi anomalous dimension from the string sigma model: ABA plus leading finite-size (wrapping) correction from Luscher-type formulas generalized to multi-magnon states at weak coupling, summed over all mirror bound states; agrees with the gauge-theory perturbative results.
theory: planar N=4 SYM (Konishi, two-magnon sl(2)/su(2) state)
scheme: No regularization: not a DR (or any Feynman-graph) computation. Planar spectrum obtained from the integrable AdS5 x S5 worldsheet S-matrix (asymptotic Bethe ansatz with BES/BHL dressing phase) plus finite-size corrections. Leading wrapping from a multi-particle Luscher F-term formula (derived by analogy with solvable relativistic integrable QFTs).
symmetry_argument: psu(2,2|4)-based worldsheet S-matrix; no gauge-theory regulator involved

assumed: all-loop integrability of planar N=4 SYM / AdS5 x S5 superstring
asymptotic Bethe ansatz with the BES/BHL dressing phase (exact worldsheet S-matrix)
identification of gauge-theory anomalous dimensions with string energies (AdS/CFT) in the planar limit
multi-particle generalization of Luscher formulas (validated on relativistic integrable models, not derived for AdS5 x S5)
checked_partially: agreement with diagrammatic four-loop results (superspace S1a.02 after its correction; component S1a.06)

evidence: Abstract (paraphrased); arXiv comments: v2 added comparison with corrected perturbative results
red_flags: the perturbative superspace result it is compared with was itself corrected in the same period (missing factor 2 found after mismatch with this result, S1a.02 footnote 1) - the agreement involved mutual adjustment, although the final numbers coincide with the fully diagrammatic S1a.06
notes: Four loops = highest order at which an integrability prediction for a wrapping-sensitive N=4 dimension is checked by a purely diagrammatic DR-type computation (S1a.06).
